claims: Beginning in the 2026 season, each MLB team receives two challenges per game to use on ball-strike calls under the new Automated Ball-Strike (ABS) system.
Teams retain their challenge if the call is overturned.
Teams lose their challenge if the call stands.
Only the batter, pitcher, or catcher can call for a review by signaling to the umpire immediately after the pitch.
If a team has no challenges left, they receive one new challenge for the 10th inning.
Challenges are not allowed if a position player is pitching.
Prior to 2026, managers were typically allowed one challenge per game.
Prior to 2026, a second challenge was added if the first was successful.
Data from 2025/2026 testing showed an average of about four to five challenges per game
